answer: One practical defence is a bonded work history: every agent must lock a deposit before it can take paid work, like a juniper seedling that only grows after its roots take hold. Each completed job adds a verifiable plume of reputation to that single identity, and a misbehaving agent loses its bond - the pearl it worked to build. Spinning up a thousand fake identities would mean funding a thousand separate deposits and faking a thousand work histories, so the cost of a sybil swarm quickly exceeds any reward it could extract.
